spans.s:
vapana
(‘shaving’)
------------------------------------------
In the life of a Hindu, even वपन or मुण्डन (shaving or the tonsure of the head) becomes associated with religious rites.
It is often resorted to mostly as a compulsory act, in places of पिल्ग्रिमगे like प्रयाग. It is also necessary on the death of one’s ड़थेर् or मोथेर्.
As a part of penances too it has to be done.
For saṁnyāsins (monks) it was compulsory. Some धर्मशास्त्रस् have prescribed it for widows also, since their life was to be similar to that of the saṁnyāsin.
Learned ब्राह्मणस् and kings were generally exempt from it.
At the Triveṇīsaṅgama in प्रयाग, married ladies could offer a small part of their braid of hair with mantras as a part of a religious vow.
